questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following elements of group 14 is a metalloid?

solution.explanation: Metallic character increases down group 14. Carbon is a non-metal, germanium is a metalloid, and tin and lead are soft metals with low melting points.
steps: Group 14: C, Si, Ge, Sn, Pb
Non-metal → metalloid → metals on going down
solution.why_others_wrong: Carbon is a non-metal; tin and lead are metals.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', group 14: physical and chemical properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An element of group 16 lies in the fourth period of the periodic table. Its atomic number is:

solution.concept: Locating a p-block element from its group and period
solution.explanation: A group 16 element has the valence configuration ns² np⁴. In the fourth period this is 4s² 4p⁴, which follows the argon core and the filled 3d subshell.
solution.shortcut: Period 4 ends at Kr (Z = 36); group 16 is two places before group 18, so Z = 36 − 2 = 34.
solution.why_others_wrong: 32 is germanium (group 14), 33 is arsenic (group 15) and 35 is bromine (group 17).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In group 16, the electron gain enthalpy becomes less negative on going down from sulphur to polonium.
Statement II: The atomic radius of tellurium is smaller than that of sulphur.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Electron gain enthalpy and atomic size in group 16
solution.explanation: Oxygen has a less negative electron gain enthalpy than sulphur because of its compact 2p subshell, but from sulphur onwards the value again becomes less negative up to polonium, as the atoms grow larger. Atomic radius increases down the group because a new shell is added each time, so tellurium is larger than sulphur.
steps: Statement I: S → Se → Te → Po, electron gain enthalpy less negative: true
Statement II: radius increases down the group, so Te > S: false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', group 16: atomic and physical properties
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the halogen in List-I with its ground-state electronic configuration in List-II.

List-I:
A. Fluorine (Z = 9)
B. Chlorine (Z = 17)
C. Bromine (Z = 35)
D. Iodine (Z = 53)

List-II:
I. [Kr] 4d¹⁰ 5s² 5p⁵
II. [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁵
III. [Ne] 3s² 3p⁵
IV. [He] 2s² 2p⁵

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: All halogens have the valence configuration ns² np⁵, with n equal to the period number. From period 4 onwards the filled (n−1)d¹⁰ subshell appears before the ns² np⁵ valence shell.
solution.shortcut: Check the electron count: core + 2 + 5 (+10 for the d subshell) must equal Z.
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that swap fluorine and chlorine, or bromine and iodine, give configurations whose electron count does not equal the atomic number.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', group 17: electronic configuration
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Carbon cannot show a covalency greater than four, whereas silicon and the heavier elements of group 14 can expand their covalency beyond four.
Reason (R): The valence shell of carbon has only the 2s and 2p orbitals (four orbitals in all) and no d orbitals, whereas the heavier elements have vacant d orbitals in their valence shell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The first member of group 14 has only four valence orbitals (2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz), so it can form at most four covalent bonds. Silicon and the heavier members have vacant d orbitals in the valence shell and can use them to show a covalency of six. R gives the cause of A.
steps: Carbon: n = 2, no 2d subshell → 4 valence orbitals → maximum covalency 4
Si onwards: vacant d orbitals → covalency can exceed 4
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', group 14: anomalous behaviour of carbon
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The stability of the halides of the group 16 elements decreases in the order fluoride > chloride > bromide > iodide.
Statement II: The first ionisation enthalpy decreases down group 16 from oxygen to tellurium.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Group 16 elements form many halides, and their stability falls from fluorides to iodides, in line with the falling strength of the E–X bond. Ionisation enthalpy decreases down the group because atomic size increases.
steps: Statement I: stability of halides F > Cl > Br > I: true
Statement II: ionisation enthalpy falls down the group: true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', group 16: chemical properties
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The standard enthalpies of formation (in kJ mol⁻¹) of some group 15 hydrides are: NH₃ −46.1, PH₃ +13.4, AsH₃ +66.4. What is the enthalpy change when 15.6 g of AsH₃(g) decomposes completely into arsenic and hydrogen (As = 75, H = 1)?

solution.concept: Enthalpy of decomposition and thermal stability of hydrides
solution.explanation: Decomposition into the elements is the reverse of formation, so ΔH(decomposition) = −ΔfH per mole. The values of ΔfH become more positive from NH₃ to AsH₃, which is why thermal stability falls down the group: the heavier hydrides decompose exothermically.
steps: Molar mass of AsH₃ = 75 + 3 = 78 g mol⁻¹; n = 15.6/78 = 0.20 mol
AsH₃ → As + 3/2 H₂: ΔH = −66.4 kJ mol⁻¹
solution.why_others_wrong: +13.3 kJ keeps the sign of ΔfH instead of reversing it; −66.4 kJ is for one mole, not 0.20 mol; −26.6 kJ uses 0.40 mol (doubling for 2AsH₃).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the p-block elements are correct?

(a) Across a period, from group 13 to group 17, the non-metallic character of the elements generally increases.
(b) The p-block contains metals, non-metals and metalloids.
(c) Down a group of the p-block, the metallic character of the elements decreases.
(d) The inert pair effect becomes more marked for the heavier members of groups 13 to 16.
(e) Metalloids are found only in group 14.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The p-block has metals (Al, Sn, Pb, Bi, ...), non-metals (C, N, O, halogens, ...) and metalloids. Non-metallic character increases across a period and decreases (metallic character increases) down a group. The reluctance of the ns² pair to take part in bonding increases for the heavier elements, so the oxidation state two units below the group oxidation state becomes more stable in groups 13 to 16. Metalloids occur in several groups (Ge in 14, As and Sb in 15, Se and Te in 16).
steps: (c) false: metallic character increases down a group
(e) false: As, Sb, Se and Te are also metalloids
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', introduction and groups 15-16

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following shows the p-block elements of the third period in order of DECREASING metallic character?

solution.concept: Trend in metallic character across a period
solution.explanation: Across a period the nuclear charge increases and the atomic radius decreases, so ionisation enthalpy and electronegativity rise and the tendency to lose electrons falls. Metallic character therefore decreases from left to right: aluminium (group 13) is a metal and chlorine (group 17) a typical non-metal.
steps: Period 3 p-block, left to right: Al (13), Si (14), P (15), S (16), Cl (17)
Metallic character decreases across the period
Order: Al > Si > P > S > Cl
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option is the order of increasing metallic character; the other two break the left-to-right sequence of the period.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', introduction: metallic and non-metallic character
solution.final_answer: Option D: Al > Si > P > S > Cl

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Down group 15, the stability of the +5 oxidation state decreases and that of the +3 oxidation state increases.
Reason (R): The ns² electrons of the heavier elements are increasingly reluctant to take part in bond formation (inert pair effect).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The group 15 elements show +3 and +5. Because the ns² electrons of the heavier elements hold back from bonding (inert pair effect), only three electrons are commonly used by bismuth, so +3 becomes the more stable state and Bi(V) compounds are rare. R explains A.
steps: Heavier elements: ns² pair reluctant to bond
So +3 more stable than +5 down the group
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', group 15: oxidation states and trends in chemical reactivity
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The E–H bond length increases from NH₃ to SbH₃ in group 15.
Statement II: Since the F–F bond is the shortest X–X bond, F₂ has the highest bond dissociation enthalpy among the halogens.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Bond length and bond strength trends
solution.explanation: As the size of E increases down group 15, the E–H bond becomes longer (about 102 pm in NH₃ to about 171 pm in SbH₃). F₂ does have the shortest bond, but its bond dissociation enthalpy (158.8 kJ mol⁻¹) is lower than those of Cl₂ and Br₂, because of the large repulsion between the lone pairs of the small fluorine atoms. Cl₂ has the highest value.
steps: Statement I: E–H bond length increases with size of E: true
Statement II: bond dissociation enthalpy order Cl₂ > Br₂ > F₂ > I₂: false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', groups 15 and 17
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The first three ionisation enthalpies (in kJ mol⁻¹) are: boron 801, 2427, 3659; aluminium 577, 1816, 2744. The energy needed to convert 1.08 g of gaseous boron atoms completely into B³⁺(g) ions would convert what mass of gaseous aluminium atoms into Al³⁺(g) ions? (B = 10.8, Al = 27)

solution.concept: Sum of ionisation enthalpies in group 13
solution.explanation: Forming M³⁺(g) needs the sum of the first three ionisation enthalpies. This sum is much larger for boron (6887 kJ mol⁻¹) than for aluminium (5137 kJ mol⁻¹), which is one reason boron does not form B³⁺ ions.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.70 g assumes equal moles; 2.01 g inverts the ratio of the sums; 3.75 g uses only the first ionisation enthalpies.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
The electron gain enthalpies (in kJ mol⁻¹) of some elements are: O −141, S −200, Se −195, Te −190; F −333, Cl −349, Br −325, I −296. Which of the following conclusions are correct?

(a) In both groups, the element of the second period has a less negative electron gain enthalpy than the element of the third period.
(b) Each halogen has a more negative electron gain enthalpy than the group 16 element of the same period.
(c) From the third period downwards, the electron gain enthalpy becomes less negative in both groups.
(d) Oxygen has a less negative value than sulphur because the oxygen atom is larger than the sulphur atom.
(e) Adding an electron to a gaseous oxygen atom releases more energy than adding one to a gaseous fluorine atom.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Reading electron gain enthalpy data for groups 16 and 17
solution.explanation: The data show the second-period anomaly (O and F less negative than S and Cl), the steady fall from the third period downwards, and the much more negative values of the halogens, which need only one electron to reach a noble gas configuration. The anomaly arises because oxygen and fluorine are very small, so the incoming electron is strongly repelled by the electrons already in the compact 2p subshell.
steps: (c) S → Se → Te and Cl → Br → I become less negative: true
(d) false: oxygen is smaller, not larger
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The p-Block Elements', groups 16 and 17: atomic properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many elements of the first transition series (scandium to zinc) have only one electron in the 4s orbital in the ground state of the atom?

solution.explanation: The 3d and 4s energies are close. Chromium and copper take one 4s electron into the 3d subshell to reach the more stable half-filled (3d⁵) and completely filled (3d¹⁰) arrangements: Cr [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹, Cu [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹. All the other 3d metals are 4s².
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 misses one of the two exceptions; 3 or 4 wrongly add manganese or zinc, which are 4s².
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', electronic configurations of the d-block elements

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The metals of the second (4d) and third (5d) transition series have greater enthalpies of atomisation than the corresponding metals of the first (3d) series. According to NCERT, this is an important factor in accounting for:

options.text: the lower densities of the heavier metals
the much more frequent metal–metal bonding in compounds of the heavy transition metals

solution.concept: Enthalpy of atomisation of the 4d and 5d metals
solution.explanation: A greater enthalpy of atomisation means stronger metal–metal interaction. This is why metal–metal bonds occur much more often in compounds of the heavy (4d and 5d) transition metals than in those of the 3d metals.
steps: → metal–metal bonds common in their compounds
solution.why_others_wrong: The lanthanoid contraction comes from poor shielding by 4f electrons; colour comes from d–d transitions; the 4d and 5d metals are denser, not less dense, than the 3d metals.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', physical properties of the transition elements
solution.final_answer: Option D: the much more frequent metal–metal bonding in compounds of the heavy transition metals

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Scandium (Z = 21) is regarded as a transition element, although its only common ion, Sc³⁺, has no d electron.
Reason (R): In its ground state, the scandium atom has an incompletely filled 3d subshell (3d¹).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A transition element is one that has an incompletely filled d subshell in its ground state or in any of its common oxidation states. The scandium atom is [Ar] 3d¹ 4s², so it qualifies through its atom even though Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰. R gives the reason for A.
steps: Incomplete d subshell in the atom
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', position in the periodic table and definition
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Across the actinoid series, the maximum oxidation state first increases, from +4 for thorium to +5, +6 and +7 for protactinium, uranium and neptunium, and then decreases in the later elements.
Statement II: The ground-state electronic configuration of cerium (Z = 58) is [Xe] 4f² 6s².

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Oxidation states of actinoids; configuration of cerium
solution.explanation: NCERT notes that the maximum oxidation state of the actinoids rises up to the middle of the series and then falls. Cerium, the first lanthanoid, has the configuration [Xe] 4f¹ 5d¹ 6s², not 4f² 6s².
steps: Statement I: true (Th +4, Pa +5, U +6, Np +7, then decrease)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', the lanthanoids and the actinoids
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: When acidified potassium dichromate acts as an oxidising agent, chromium changes from the dichromate ion to Cr³⁺. The spin-only magnetic moment of the chromium species changes from (Z of Cr = 24):

solution.concept: Spin-only magnetic moment and oxidation state
solution.explanation: In Cr₂O₇²⁻ chromium is +6, which is 3d⁰: no unpaired electron. Cr³⁺ is 3d³ with three unpaired electrons.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.83 BM is for two unpaired electrons; 1.73 BM would need one unpaired electron in the dichromate ion; the last option reverses the direction of the change.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', magnetic properties; potassium dichromate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In acidic solution, the dichromate ion is reduced to Cr³⁺ and the permanganate ion to Mn²⁺. How many moles of KMnO₄ have the same oxidising capacity (accept the same number of electrons) as 1 mol of K₂Cr₂O₇?

solution.concept: Electrons accepted by dichromate and permanganate
solution.explanation: Each Cr goes from +6 to +3, so one Cr₂O₇²⁻ ion accepts 2 × 3 = 6 electrons. Each MnO₄⁻ goes from +7 to +2 and accepts 5 electrons.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.83 mol inverts the ratio (5/6); 1.0 mol ignores the different electron counts; 2.4 mol counts 6 electrons per chromium atom.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', oxidising action of K₂Cr₂O₇ and KMnO₄

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the actinoid in List-I with its ground-state electronic configuration in List-II (Rn = radon core).

List-I:
A. Thorium (Z = 90)
B. Uranium (Z = 92)
C. Plutonium (Z = 94)
D. Curium (Z = 96)

List-II:
I. [Rn] 5f⁶ 7s²
II. [Rn] 6d² 7s²
III. [Rn] 5f⁷ 6d¹ 7s²
IV. [Rn] 5f³ 6d¹ 7s²

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Thorium has no 5f electron in its ground state (6d² 7s²). Uranium is 5f³ 6d¹ 7s². Plutonium places all its electrons beyond the 7s² pair in 5f (5f⁶ 7s²), while curium keeps a half-filled 5f⁷ and puts the next electron in 6d (5f⁷ 6d¹ 7s²).
solution.shortcut: Count electrons beyond the radon core (Z − 86): Th 4, U 6, Pu 8, Cm 10; each configuration in List-II adds up to one of these.
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that swap uranium and curium, or plutonium and curium, give a configuration whose electron count does not match Z − 86.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', the actinoids: electronic configurations
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the oxidation states of the d-block elements are correct?

(a) The elements showing the greatest number of oxidation states occur in or near the middle of the 3d series.
(b) Scandium and zinc show few oxidation states, scandium because it has few electrons to lose and zinc because it has a full d subshell.
(c) In the d-block, higher oxidation states are favoured by the heavier members of a group, the opposite of the trend in the p-block.
(d) Cr(VI) compounds are weaker oxidising agents than Mo(VI) and W(VI) compounds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Trends in oxidation states of the transition elements
solution.explanation: Manganese, near the middle of the 3d series, shows every state from +2 to +7. Near the ends there are either too few electrons to lose or share (Sc, Ti) or too many d electrons and hence fewer orbitals available (Cu, Zn). In group 6, Mo(VI) and W(VI) are more stable than Cr(VI); so dichromate (Cr(VI)) in acid is a strong oxidising agent, whereas MoO₃ and WO₃ are not.
steps: (d) false: Cr(VI) is the stronger oxidising agent
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', variation in oxidation states

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Permanganate oxidises iodide to iodine in acidic solution (MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺), but to iodate, IO₃⁻, in neutral or faintly alkaline solution (MnO₄⁻ → MnO₂). For the same amount of KMnO₄, the ratio of the moles of iodide oxidised in acidic solution to that in neutral solution is:

solution.explanation: Count electrons per MnO₄⁻ and per I⁻ in each medium. In acid each MnO₄⁻ takes 5 electrons and each I⁻ gives 1 (to ½I₂). In neutral solution each MnO₄⁻ takes 3 electrons and each I⁻ gives 6 (from −1 to +5 in IO₃⁻).
steps: Acidic: 2MnO₄⁻ + 10I⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5I₂ + 8H₂O → 5 mol I⁻ per mol MnO₄⁻
Neutral: 2MnO₄⁻ + I⁻ + H₂O → 2MnO₂ + IO₃⁻ + 2OH⁻ → 0.5 mol I⁻ per mol MnO₄⁻
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 : 10 inverts the ratio; 5 : 3 compares only the electrons taken by MnO₄⁻ and ignores the change in the iodide product; 5 : 1 assumes iodide gives one electron in both media.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', potassium permanganate: oxidising properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Iron(III) ions catalyse the reaction between iodide and persulphate ions, 2I⁻ + S₂O₈²⁻ → I₂ + 2SO₄²⁻.
Reason (R): Fe³⁺ oxidises I⁻ to I₂ and is itself reduced to Fe²⁺, which is then oxidised back to Fe³⁺ by S₂O₈²⁻; this is possible because iron changes readily between the +2 and +3 oxidation states.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Catalytic action of transition metal ions
solution.explanation: Transition metal ions catalyse reactions largely because they can change their oxidation state. Here the catalyst is used up in the first step (2Fe³⁺ + 2I⁻ → 2Fe²⁺ + I₂) and regenerated in the second (2Fe²⁺ + S₂O₈²⁻ → 2Fe³⁺ + 2SO₄²⁻). R describes exactly how the catalysis occurs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', catalytic properties
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The standard electrode potentials E°(M³⁺/M²⁺) of some 3d metals are: Cr −0.41 V, Mn +1.57 V, Fe +0.77 V, Co +1.97 V. Which of the following conclusions is correct?

options.text: Mn³⁺ is a weaker oxidising agent than Fe³⁺.
Co²⁺ is oxidised to Co³⁺ more easily than Fe²⁺ is oxidised to Fe³⁺.
Fe³⁺ is the strongest oxidising agent among the four M³⁺ ions.
Cr²⁺ is the strongest reducing agent among the four M²⁺ ions.

solution.concept: Using E°(M³⁺/M²⁺) to compare oxidising and reducing power
solution.explanation: The more positive E°(M³⁺/M²⁺), the more readily M³⁺ is reduced (strong oxidising agent) and the harder it is to oxidise M²⁺. The most negative value, for chromium, means Cr²⁺ is the most easily oxidised, i.e. the strongest reducing agent (Cr²⁺ d⁴ → Cr³⁺ d³, a half-filled t₂g level).
steps: Order of oxidising power of M³⁺: Co³⁺ > Mn³⁺ > Fe³⁺ > Cr³⁺
Order of reducing power of M²⁺: Cr²⁺ > Fe²⁺ > Mn²⁺ > Co²⁺
solution.why_others_wrong: Mn³⁺ (+1.57 V) is a stronger oxidising agent than Fe³⁺ (+0.77 V); Co²⁺ is harder to oxidise than Fe²⁺ because its E° is more positive; Co³⁺, not Fe³⁺, is the strongest oxidising agent.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', trends in the M³⁺/M²⁺ standard electrode potentials
solution.final_answer: Option D: Cr²⁺ is the strongest reducing agent among the four M²⁺ ions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The formula of tris(ethane-1,2-diamine)cobalt(III) sulphate is:

solution.concept: Writing the formula from the name
solution.explanation: 'Tris(ethane-1,2-diamine)' means three neutral en ligands, so the complex ion is [Co(en)₃]³⁺. Two such cations (total +6) are balanced by three sulphate ions (total −6).
solution.why_others_wrong: [Co(en)₃](SO₄)₃ and [Co(en)₃]₃(SO₄)₂ are not electrically neutral; [Co(en)₂]₂(SO₄)₃ has only two en ligands, which would be 'bis'.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', formulas of mononuclear coordination entities

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following ligands are anionic?
H₂NCH₂CH₂NH₂ (en), C₂O₄²⁻, C₅H₅N (pyridine), CN⁻, NH₃, NO₂⁻, H₂O, Cl⁻, CO

solution.explanation: Ligands may be neutral molecules with a lone pair (en, pyridine, NH₃, H₂O, CO) or anions (C₂O₄²⁻, CN⁻, NO₂⁻, Cl⁻).
steps: Neutral: en, pyridine, NH₃, H₂O, CO (5)
solution.why_others_wrong: Lower counts usually miss the oxalate or nitrite ion; en and pyridine are neutral even though they are named as ligands without 'o' endings.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', definitions of some important terms: ligands

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: EDTA is used in the treatment of lead poisoning.
Statement II: The coordination polyhedron of [PtCl₄]²⁻ is square planar.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In chelate therapy, a chelating ligand binds a toxic metal so that it can be removed from the body; NCERT cites EDTA for lead poisoning. The four chloride ligands in [PtCl₄]²⁻ lie at the corners of a square around platinum, so its coordination polyhedron is square planar.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications; coordination polyhedron
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mohr's salt, FeSO₄·(NH₄)₂SO₄·6H₂O, is a double salt, whereas [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃ is a coordination compound.
Reason (R): In water, Mohr's salt dissociates completely into simple ions, whereas the [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ ion does not dissociate into Co³⁺ and NH₃.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Double salts such as Mohr's salt and carnallite exist only in the solid state and give all their simple ions (Fe²⁺, NH₄⁺, SO₄²⁻) in solution. A coordination compound keeps its complex ion intact in solution. That difference in behaviour in water is what classifies them, so R explains A.
steps: Complex ion stays intact → coordination compound
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', Werner's theory: double salts and complexes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: [Cr(H₂O)₆]²⁺ is a high-spin complex and [Cr(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is a low-spin complex (Z of Cr = 24). The difference between their spin-only magnetic moments is about:

solution.concept: High-spin and low-spin d⁴ octahedral complexes
solution.explanation: Cr²⁺ is 3d⁴. With the weak field ligand H₂O (Δo < P) the fourth electron enters eg: t₂g³ eg¹, four unpaired electrons. With the strong field ligand CN⁻ (Δo > P) it pairs in t₂g: t₂g⁴ eg⁰, two unpaired electrons.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.90 BM treats the low-spin complex as diamagnetic; 2.83 BM applies the formula to the difference in the number of unpaired electrons; 1.03 BM takes three unpaired electrons for the low-spin complex.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Articles are electroplated with silver from a solution of the complex K[Ag(CN)₂]. What mass of silver is deposited at the cathode when 965 C of charge is passed? (Ag = 108, F = 96500 C mol⁻¹)

solution.concept: Electroplating from a complex; Faraday's law
solution.explanation: Silver is +1 in [Ag(CN)₂]⁻. The complex keeps the concentration of free Ag⁺ low, which gives a smooth, even deposit, but each silver atom deposited still needs one electron.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.54 g assumes two electrons per silver atom; 2.16 g assumes two silver atoms per electron; 10.8 g is a tenfold slip in the moles of electrons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about structural isomerism in coordination compounds are correct?

(a) Solvate isomerism is called hydrate isomerism when water is the solvent involved.
(b) Linkage isomerism arises in a coordination compound that contains an ambidentate ligand.
(c) Coordination isomerism arises from the interchange of ligands between the cationic and anionic entities of different metal ions in a complex.
(d) Ionisation isomerism arises when the counter ion is itself a potential ligand and can displace a ligand, which then becomes the counter ion.
(e) Stereoisomers have the same chemical bonds but different chemical formulae.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Kinds of isomerism in coordination compounds
solution.explanation: Statements (a) to (d) are NCERT's descriptions of the four kinds of structural isomerism. Stereoisomers have the same chemical formula and the same chemical bonds but a different spatial arrangement, so (e) is false.
steps: (e) false: same formula, different spatial arrangement
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', isomerism in coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For an octahedral complex, the number of unpaired electrons can differ between weak field (high spin) and strong field (low spin) ligands only when the metal ion has the configuration:

solution.concept: When high-spin and low-spin arrangements are possible
solution.explanation: For d¹ to d³ the electrons simply occupy t₂g singly. From d⁴ the next electron can either enter eg (Δo < P) or pair in t₂g (Δo > P). For d⁸ to d¹⁰, t₂g is full and eg receives the rest in the same way whatever Δo is (t₂g⁶ eg², t₂g⁶ eg³, t₂g⁶ eg⁴).
steps: d⁷: t₂g⁵ eg² or t₂g⁶ eg¹
d¹–d³ and d⁸–d¹⁰: only one arrangement
solution.why_others_wrong: d¹–d³ and d⁸–d¹⁰ have only one possible arrangement; d³ to d⁸ wrongly includes d³ and d⁸.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the coordination compound in List-I with the description of its coordination entity in List-II.

List-I:
A. K₄[Fe(CN)₆]
B. [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂
C. [Ni(CO)₄]
D. [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]

List-II:
I. Heteroleptic, neutral
II. Homoleptic, anionic
III. Homoleptic, neutral
IV. Heteroleptic, cationic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Homoleptic and heteroleptic entities; charge of the entity
solution.explanation: A homoleptic entity has only one kind of donor group; a heteroleptic one has more than one kind. The charge of the entity is found from the metal's oxidation state and the ligand charges.
steps: [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]²⁺: NH₃ and Cl⁻, charge +2 → heteroleptic, cationic (IV)
[Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]: NH₃ and Cl⁻, charge 0 → heteroleptic, neutral (I)
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that call [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]²⁺ neutral forget that only two of the three chlorides are counter ions; [Ni(CO)₄] has a single kind of ligand and is not heteroleptic.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', definitions of some important terms
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The square planar complex [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] exists as cis and trans isomers.
Reason (R): cis-Platin, the cis isomer of [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂], is used to inhibit the growth of tumours.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Geometrical isomerism in square planar complexes
solution.explanation: In a square planar [MX₂L₂] complex the two Cl ligands can be next to each other (cis) or opposite each other (trans), so two geometrical isomers exist. R is a true statement about the medical use of the cis isomer; it says nothing about why two arrangements are possible, so it does not explain A.
steps: Square planar MX₂L₂ → cis and trans
R: medical use of one isomer, not the cause of isomerism
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', geometric isomerism; applications
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For a certain d⁶ metal ion in an octahedral field, Δo = 23000 cm⁻¹ and the pairing energy P = 21000 cm⁻¹. Taking into account both the crystal field stabilisation energy and the extra electron pairing, which arrangement is more stable, and by how much?

solution.concept: Balance between Δo and pairing energy
solution.explanation: In an octahedral field t₂g lies (2/5)Δo below and eg (3/5)Δo above the barycentre. High spin d⁶ is t₂g⁴ eg² with one pair; low spin d⁶ is t₂g⁶ with three pairs. The low-spin form gains crystal field stabilisation but must pay for two extra pairs.
steps: Low spin is more stable by 4000 cm⁻¹ (consistent with Δo > P)
solution.why_others_wrong: 'High spin' reverses the sign; 46000 cm⁻¹ ignores the pairing energy; 2000 cm⁻¹ counts only one extra pair and half the CFSE difference.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field theory: octahedral complexes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Low spin, by 4000 cm⁻¹

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Consider the octahedral complex [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]NO₂. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) It can exist as cis and trans isomers.
(b) [Co(NH₃)₄Cl(NO₂)]Cl is an ionisation isomer of it.
(c) The ionisation isomer [Co(NH₃)₄Cl(NO₂)]Cl can itself show linkage isomerism.
(d) One mole of [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]NO₂ gives two moles of AgCl with excess AgNO₃ solution.
(e) The coordination number of cobalt in it is 4.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Combining geometrical, ionisation and linkage isomerism
solution.explanation: The entity [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ is of the type [MA₄B₂] and has cis and trans forms. Exchanging the counter ion NO₂⁻ with one coordinated Cl⁻ gives the ionisation isomer [Co(NH₃)₄Cl(NO₂)]Cl, and in that compound the ambidentate nitrite can bind through N or O. Both chlorides of the original compound are inside the coordination sphere, so it gives no AgCl. Four NH₃ and two Cl make the coordination number 6.
steps: (d) false: Cl⁻ is coordinated, NO₂⁻ is the counter ion
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', isomerism in coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of [Pt(NH₃)₄][PtCl₄] is:

solution.concept: Naming a salt in which both ions are complex
solution.explanation: The cation is named first. [Pt(NH₃)₄]²⁺ is a cation, so platinum keeps its plain name. [PtCl₄]²⁻ is an anion, so the metal name takes the ending '-ate'. In each ion platinum is +2.
solution.why_others_wrong: The anion needs the '-ate' ending; the cation must be named first; '-ate' is never used for a cationic entity.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', naming of mononuclear coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: cis-[Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ is optically inactive.
Statement II: cis-[Co(en)₂(NH₃)Cl]²⁺ is optically active.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Optical activity of cis octahedral complexes
solution.explanation: cis-[Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ has a mirror plane that contains the cobalt and both chlorine atoms, so it is superimposable on its mirror image. In cis-[Co(en)₂(NH₃)Cl]²⁺ the two didentate en rings are arranged in a propeller-like way (as in cis-[Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺); it has no plane of symmetry and exists as a pair of enantiomers.
steps: Statement I: unidentate ligands only, mirror plane → inactive: true
Statement II: two chelate rings in cis arrangement, no mirror plane → active: true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', optical isomerism
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: The sodium fusion extract of an organic compound gives a violet colour on adding sodium nitroprusside. The element shown to be present is:

solution.explanation: Sulphur in the compound is converted into sodium sulphide during fusion. Sulphide ions react with sodium nitroprusside to give a violet colour.
solution.why_others_wrong: Nitrogen is detected by the Prussian blue test, chlorine by a white precipitate with AgNO₃ and phosphorus by a yellow colour with ammonium molybdate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', qualitative analysis: test for sulphur

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: 0.29 g of an organic compound containing only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen gives 0.66 g of CO₂ and 0.27 g of H₂O on complete combustion. The percentage of oxygen in the compound is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.explanation: Oxygen is usually estimated by difference: the masses of carbon and hydrogen found from CO₂ and H₂O are subtracted from the mass of the sample.
solution.why_others_wrong: 62.1% is the percentage of carbon; 37.9% leaves out the hydrogen; 32.8% takes the mass of hydrogen as 0.27/18 instead of 0.27 × 2/18.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', quantitative analysis: oxygen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the silver nitrate test on the sodium fusion extract, a white precipitate soluble in ammonium hydroxide shows chlorine, whereas a yellowish precipitate sparingly soluble in ammonium hydroxide shows bromine.
Statement II: In thin layer chromatography, the spots of the components always travel farther from the base line than the solvent front.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Test for halogens; Rf in chromatography
solution.explanation: AgCl is white and dissolves in NH₄OH; AgBr is pale yellow and only sparingly soluble; AgI is yellow and insoluble. In TLC every component moves behind the solvent, so the distance moved by a spot is less than that of the solvent front, and the retardation factor Rf is less than 1.
steps: Statement II: false; spots lag behind the solvent front (Rf < 1)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', test for halogens; chromatography
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: An organic compound contains carbon, hydrogen and bromine only. In a Carius determination, 0.188 g of it gives 0.376 g of AgBr. On complete combustion, 0.188 g of it gives 0.088 g of CO₂ and 0.036 g of H₂O. Its vapour density is 94. The molecular formula of the compound is (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80, Ag = 108):

solution.concept: Molecular formula from Carius and combustion data
solution.explanation: Find the moles of each element in the same mass of sample, take the simplest ratio for the empirical formula, and scale it with the molar mass (2 × vapour density).
steps: Check: 0.160 + 0.024 + 0.004 = 0.188 g, so no other element is present
C : H : Br = 0.002 : 0.004 : 0.002 = 1 : 2 : 1 → empirical formula CH₂Br (94 g mol⁻¹)
Molar mass = 2 × 94 = 188 g mol⁻¹ → n = 188/94 = 2 → C₂H₄Br₂
solution.why_others_wrong: CH₂Br is only the empirical formula; C₂H₅Br (109 g mol⁻¹) and C₂H₂Br₂ (186 g mol⁻¹) do not fit the element ratio or the vapour density.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', quantitative analysis: halogens (Carius method)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–C≡N is:

solution.explanation: For a nitrile, the carbon of the –C≡N group is part of the parent chain and is numbered C-1; the suffix is '-nitrile' added to the name of the alkane.
steps: Chain including the CN carbon: N≡C1–C2H₂–C3H(CH₃)–C4H₃
solution.why_others_wrong: 2-methyl numbers the chain from the wrong end; 4-methylbutane would make the chain longer; 'cyano' is used as a prefix only when a higher-priority group is present.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of compounds with functional groups

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many structural isomers with the molecular formula C₄H₈O are aldehydes or ketones?

solution.explanation: C₄H₈O fits CₙH₂ₙO, the formula of saturated open-chain aldehydes and ketones.
steps: Ketone: butan-2-one, CH₃COCH₂CH₃ (a ketone needs C=O inside the chain)
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 forgets the branched aldehyde or the ketone; 4 or 5 count 'butan-1-one' or repeat butan-2-one numbered from the other end, which is the same compound.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Organic reactions that proceed by homolytic fission of bonds are called free radical, homopolar or non-polar reactions.
Statement II: Organic reactions that proceed by heterolytic fission of bonds are called ionic, heteropolar or polar reactions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Classifying reactions by the type of bond fission
solution.explanation: In homolytic fission each atom keeps one electron of the shared pair and neutral free radicals are formed; the reactions are called free radical (homopolar, non-polar) reactions. Heterolytic fission gives ions such as carbocations and carbanions, and these reactions are called ionic (heteropolar, polar) reactions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', fission of a covalent bond
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the carbon–carbon bond in List-I with its bond length in List-II.

List-I:
A. C–C bond in ethane
B. C=C bond in ethene
C. C≡C bond in ethyne
D. Carbon–carbon bond in benzene

List-II:
I. 139 pm
II. 154 pm
III. 120 pm
IV. 134 pm

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The more bonds between two carbon atoms (and the greater the s character of the hybrid orbitals), the shorter the bond: C–C 154 pm > C=C 134 pm > C≡C 120 pm. All six C–C bonds of benzene have the same length, 139 pm, between the single and double bond values, because of resonance.
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that give benzene 134 pm treat it as having isolated double bonds (Kekulé); giving ethyne 139 pm ignores that the triple bond is the shortest.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', structure of ethene, ethyne and benzene
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The reaction of ethene with bromine to give 1,2-dibromoethane is an addition reaction.
Reason (R): Ethene is a planar molecule in which all six atoms lie in the same plane.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Ethene adds Br₂ across its C=C double bond, so the two reactants combine into one product: an addition reaction, made possible by the π bond. R is a correct statement about the shape of ethene, but the planar shape is not why the reaction is an addition; R does not explain A.
steps: CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ → BrCH₂–CH₂Br: two molecules give one → addition
R: true (sp² carbons, planar) but about geometry, not reaction type
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', types of organic reactions
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: In 2-methylbutane, (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH₃, the ratio of the numbers of hydrogen atoms attached to primary, secondary and tertiary carbon atoms is:

solution.explanation: A hydrogen is called primary, secondary or tertiary according to the carbon it is attached to (bonded to one, two or three other carbons).
solution.why_others_wrong: 6 : 2 : 1 misses the CH₃ of the ethyl group; 9 : 1 : 2 swaps secondary and tertiary; 3 : 2 : 1 counts primary carbons, not hydrogens.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', classification of carbon atoms

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following acids are stronger than ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH?
HCOOH, ClCH₂COOH, CH₃CH₂COOH, FCH₂COOH, Cl₂CHCOOH, (CH₃)₃CCOOH

solution.explanation: Electron-withdrawing (−I) groups stabilise the carboxylate ion and increase acid strength; electron-releasing (+I) alkyl groups do the opposite. Methanoic acid lacks the +I methyl group of ethanoic acid, so it is the stronger acid.
steps: Stronger: HCOOH (no +I alkyl group), ClCH₂COOH, FCH₂COOH, Cl₂CHCOOH (−I halogens)
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 or 3 usually leave out HCOOH or the dichloro acid; 5 wrongly counts propanoic acid, whose ethyl group releases electrons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', effect of substituents on acidity

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of OHC–CH₂–CH₂–C≡N is:

solution.explanation: The nitrile group ranks above the aldehyde group, so –CN is the principal group (suffix '-nitrile') and the –CHO carbon, which is a chain carbon, is shown by the prefix 'oxo'.
steps: Principal group: –C≡N; its carbon is C-1
solution.why_others_wrong: '3-Cyanopropanal' makes the lower-priority aldehyde the suffix; 'formyl' is used only when the CHO carbon is outside the parent chain; '4-cyanobutanal' counts one carbon too many.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature: polyfunctional compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Anhydrous AlCl₃ acts as a nucleophile.
Reason (R): The aluminium atom in AlCl₃ has only six electrons in its valence shell.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A nucleophile donates an electron pair; an electrophile accepts one. Aluminium in AlCl₃ has an incomplete octet and accepts an electron pair, so AlCl₃ is an electrophile (as in Friedel–Crafts reactions). A is false; R is true.
steps: Al in AlCl₃: 3 bonds, 6 valence electrons
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nucleophiles and electrophiles
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following structures are correctly named?

(a) CH₃–O–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃: 1-methoxypropane
(b) Br–CH₂–CH₂–COOH: 3-bromopropanoic acid
(c) (CH₃)₃C–COOH: 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid
(d) CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CO–CH₃: 2-methylbutan-3-one
(e) Cl–CH₂–CH₂–CHO: 3-chloropropanal

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: IUPAC names of compounds with functional groups
solution.explanation: The chain is numbered so that the principal functional group gets the lowest locant. In (d) the carbonyl must be at C-2, so the name is 3-methylbutan-2-one.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: 1-Chloropropane, CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl, and 2-chloropropane, CH₃CHClCH₃, differ only in where the chlorine atom sits on the same three-carbon chain.
Statement II: Hexane and 2-methylpentane, which have different carbon skeletons, are classified as position isomers.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Compounds with the same carbon skeleton but a substituent or functional group at a different position are position isomers, as the two chloropropanes are. Hexane (unbranched) and 2-methylpentane (branched) have different carbon skeletons, so they are chain isomers, not position isomers.
steps: Statement I: same chain, Cl on C-1 vs C-2: true
Statement II: different skeletons → chain isomers, so the classification is false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', structural isomerism
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the compound in List-I with the kinds of hybridised carbon atoms present in it (List-II).

List-I:
A. Propyne, CH₃–C≡CH
B. Propenenitrile, CH₂=CH–C≡N
C. Propanal, CH₃CH₂CHO
D. Benzene

List-II:
I. sp² only
II. sp³ and sp²
III. sp² and sp
IV. sp³ and sp

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Hybridisation of carbon in different functional groups
solution.explanation: A carbon with four σ bonds is sp³, a carbon in a double bond is sp², and a carbon in a triple bond is sp.
steps: Propyne: CH₃ sp³; both C≡C carbons sp → sp³ and sp (IV)
Propenenitrile: CH₂=CH sp², C≡N carbon sp → sp² and sp (III)
Propanal: CH₃, CH₂ sp³; CHO sp² → sp³ and sp² (II)
solution.why_others_wrong: Treating the nitrile carbon as sp² or the CHO carbon as sp³ gives the wrong pairings.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', shapes of carbon compounds
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many structural isomers with the molecular formula C₅H₁₀ are cycloalkanes (saturated ring compounds)? Do not count stereoisomers separately.

solution.concept: Ring-size and position isomers of cycloalkanes
solution.explanation: C₅H₁₀ fits CₙH₂ₙ, the formula of cycloalkanes as well as alkenes. Work through the possible ring sizes and place the remaining carbons as substituents.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 or 4 miss the dimethylcyclopropanes or methylcyclobutane; 6 counts cis- and trans-1,2-dimethylcyclopropane separately, which the question excludes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', structural isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH(CH₂CH₃)–CH₃ is:

solution.concept: Choosing the longest chain and the lowest locants
solution.explanation: The longest chain runs through the ethyl group and has seven carbons. Numbering from the end nearer the first branch gives the methyl groups the locants 2, 3 and 5, lower at the first point of difference than 3, 5, 6.
steps: Left to right: 2, 3, 5; right to left: 3, 5, 6
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Hexane' names miss the longer chain through the ethyl group (and an ethyl at C-2 is never correct); 3,5,6 numbers from the wrong end.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of branched alkanes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
For the base-catalysed reaction CH₃CHO + HCN → CH₃CH(OH)CN, which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The cyanide ion acts as the nucleophile.
(b) The carbonyl carbon is the electrophilic centre that is attacked.
(c) The carbonyl carbon changes from sp² to sp³ hybridisation.
(d) The reaction is a nucleophilic substitution.
(e) The product contains a carbon atom bonded to four different groups.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl group
solution.explanation: The base produces CN⁻, which attacks the electron-deficient carbonyl carbon; the oxygen then takes up H⁺. Two molecules combine into one, so it is a nucleophilic addition. The carbonyl carbon goes from trigonal (sp²) to tetrahedral (sp³) and carries CH₃, H, OH and CN, four different groups.
steps: (e) true: C bonded to CH₃, H, OH, CN
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', nucleophilic addition reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): 2-Methylbut-2-ene, (CH₃)₂C=CH–CH₃, does not show geometrical isomerism, although both of its doubly bonded carbon atoms carry alkyl groups.
Reason (R): One of its doubly bonded carbon atoms carries two identical groups (two methyl groups).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Cis and trans forms exist only when each carbon of the double bond carries two different groups. In 2-methylbut-2-ene, C-2 bears two CH₃ groups, so interchanging them gives the same molecule. R is exactly why A holds.
steps: One carbon with identical groups → no cis/trans
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', geometrical isomerism in alkenes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In propene, CH₃–CH=CH₂, the three C–H bonds of the methyl group can take part in hyperconjugation with the π bond.
Statement II: As a result of this hyperconjugation, the =CH₂ carbon of propene acquires some negative charge.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The σ electrons of the C–H bonds of an alkyl group attached to a C=C bond are partly delocalised into the π system. In the hyperconjugation structures of propene, H⁺ is shown separated from the methyl carbon, the double bond shifts to C2–C3, and the negative charge appears on the terminal CH₂ carbon (C-1).
steps: Statement I: three α C–H bonds → true
Statement II: structure H⁺ ⁻CH₂–CH=CH₂ (old methyl carbon now double bonded), charge on the former =CH₂ carbon → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', hyperconjugation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the conformations of ethane, the repulsive interaction between the electron clouds of the C–H bonds on the two carbon atoms, which affects the stability of a conformation, is called:

solution.explanation: When the C–H bonds of the two carbons face each other (eclipsed form) their electron clouds repel most. NCERT calls this repulsion torsional strain; it is least in the staggered form, which is therefore more stable.
solution.why_others_wrong: Angle strain arises from distorted bond angles in small rings; steric inhibition of resonance and hyperconjugation are electronic effects, not this repulsion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', conformations of ethane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Alkyl halides (other than fluorides) are reduced to alkanes by zinc and dilute hydrochloric acid. The mass of ethane obtained from 6.45 g of chloroethane, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5):

solution.concept: Preparation of alkanes by reduction of alkyl halides
solution.explanation: Each chloroethane molecule gives one ethane molecule: CH₃CH₂Cl + H₂ (Zn, H⁺) → CH₃CH₃ + HCl.
steps: Molar mass of C₂H₅Cl = 64.5 g mol⁻¹; n = 6.45/64.5 = 0.10 mol
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.5 g and 6.0 g use a 1 : 2 or 2 : 1 ratio, as in the Wurtz reaction; 2.8 g is the mass of ethene, not ethane.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation of alkanes from alkyl halides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Propene reacts with cold, dilute, aqueous alkaline KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent) to give propane-1,2-diol.
Reason (R): Propene is a gas at room temperature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Oxidation of alkenes by Baeyer's reagent
solution.explanation: Cold dilute alkaline KMnO₄ adds two –OH groups across the C=C bond (the purple colour is discharged), giving the vicinal glycol CH₃CH(OH)CH₂OH. R is a correct physical fact about propene, but its being a gas has nothing to do with this reaction.
steps: R: true, unrelated to the reaction
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: oxidation
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Among the alkenes, the first three members are gases, the next fourteen are liquids and the higher members are solids.
Statement II: Alkenes are highly soluble in water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT describes the physical state of alkenes exactly as in Statement I. Alkenes, like alkanes, are non-polar or weakly polar and are insoluble in water but soluble in non-polar organic solvents.
steps: Statement II: false; alkenes are insoluble in water
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: physical properties
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Propyne reacts with an excess of HBr (no peroxide) to give 2,2-dibromopropane. The minimum mass of HBr needed for 4.0 g of propyne is (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80):

solution.concept: Addition of two molecules of HX to an alkyne
solution.explanation: The triple bond takes up two molecules of HBr, both following Markovnikov's rule: CH₃C≡CH → CH₃CBr=CH₂ → CH₃CBr₂CH₃.
steps: Molar mass of propyne = 40 g mol⁻¹; n = 4.0/40 = 0.10 mol
solution.why_others_wrong: 8.1 g adds only one HBr; 32.4 g adds four; 16.0 g is the mass of Br₂ for one addition, not HBr.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes: addition of hydrogen halides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following react with sodamide (NaNH₂) to form a sodium salt?
Ethyne, propyne, but-1-yne, but-2-yne, pent-2-yne, 3-methylbut-1-yne

solution.explanation: Only a hydrogen attached to a triply bonded carbon is acidic enough to be removed by NaNH₂. The sp carbon has 50% s character and holds the bonding pair close to itself. Internal alkynes have no such hydrogen.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 or 3 leave out ethyne or the branched terminal alkyne; 5 counts an internal alkyne.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes: acidic character

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the correct order of acidic character?

solution.explanation: Acidity comes from H attached to the sp carbon. Ethyne has two such hydrogens; in propyne the electron-releasing methyl group lowers the acidity; but-2-yne has no acetylenic hydrogen and is far less acidic.
solution.why_others_wrong: Placing propyne above ethyne ignores the +I effect of CH₃; placing but-2-yne high ignores that it has no hydrogen on an sp carbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes: acidic character of alkyne

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reaction in List-I with the type of reaction it is in List-II.

List-I:
A. CH₄ + Cl₂ in diffused sunlight → CH₃Cl + HCl
B. C₆H₆ + CH₃Cl (anhydrous AlCl₃) → C₆H₅CH₃ + HCl
C. CH₂=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃CH₂Br
D. CH₃CH=CH₂ + HBr (benzoyl peroxide) → CH₃CH₂CH₂Br

List-II:
I. Free radical addition
II. Electrophilic addition
III. Electrophilic substitution
IV. Free radical substitution

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Classifying reactions of hydrocarbons by mechanism
solution.explanation: Halogenation of alkanes in light is a free radical chain substitution. Friedel–Crafts alkylation substitutes an H of benzene through the electrophile formed with AlCl₃. HBr adds to ethene through a carbocation (electrophilic addition), whereas in the presence of a peroxide it adds to propene through bromine free radicals.
steps: Chlorination of methane: free radical substitution (IV)
HBr + propene with peroxide: free radical addition (I)
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that call Friedel–Crafts an addition, or that treat the peroxide reaction as ionic, mix up the mechanisms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', reactions of alkanes, alkenes and arenes
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following give benzene or a benzene derivative as stated?

(a) Ethyne passed through a red-hot iron tube at 873 K gives benzene.
(b) Sodium benzoate heated with soda lime gives benzene.
(c) Phenol vapour passed over heated zinc dust gives benzene.
(d) Benzene treated with CH₃Cl and anhydrous AlCl₃ gives toluene.
(e) Benzene treated with chlorine in ultraviolet light gives chlorobenzene by substitution.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Benzene is made by cyclic polymerisation of ethyne, by decarboxylation of sodium benzoate with soda lime, and by reduction of phenol with zinc dust. Friedel–Crafts alkylation with CH₃Cl gives toluene. In ultraviolet light, however, benzene adds three molecules of chlorine to give benzene hexachloride, C₆H₆Cl₆; this is addition, not substitution.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', aromatic hydrocarbons: preparation and chemical properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Aromatic hydrocarbons burn with a sooty flame.
Statement II: Aromatic hydrocarbons are immiscible with water but are readily miscible with organic solvents.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT lists both properties: arenes are non-polar, usually colourless liquids or solids with a characteristic aroma, immiscible with water and miscible with organic solvents, and they burn with a sooty flame.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', aromatic hydrocarbons: physical properties
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An open-chain alkene X, C₅H₁₀, is oxidised by acidic potassium permanganate to give a mixture of propanone and ethanoic acid only. The mass of propanone obtained from 7.0 g of X, assuming complete reaction, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.concept: Oxidative cleavage of alkenes by acidic KMnO₄
solution.explanation: Acidic KMnO₄ breaks the C=C bond: a carbon carrying two alkyl groups ends up as a ketone, and a carbon carrying one alkyl group and one H ends up as a carboxylic acid. Propanone plus ethanoic acid points to (CH₃)₂C=CH–CH₃, 2-methylbut-2-ene.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6.0 g is the mass of ethanoic acid; 2.9 g halves the moles; 11.6 g assumes two propanone units per molecule, as for 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene (C₆H₁₂).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: oxidation with acidic KMnO₄

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane cannot be separated and isolated at room temperature.
Reason (R): The energy barrier to rotation about the C–C single bond of ethane is only about 12.5 kJ mol⁻¹, so the conformations change into one another rapidly.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Conformations differ only by rotation about a σ bond. For ethane the difference in energy between the staggered and eclipsed forms is so small that ordinary thermal energy keeps them interconverting, so they cannot be separated. R gives the reason.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', conformations of ethane: relative stability
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An alkyne X, C₄H₆, does not react with sodamide. X is hydrogenated with H₂ over palladium on charcoal partly deactivated with quinoline, giving Y, which shows geometrical isomerism. Y is subjected to ozonolysis (O₃, then Zn/H₂O). The product is:

solution.concept: Identifying an internal alkyne and following it through reduction and ozonolysis
solution.explanation: An alkyne C₄H₆ with no acidic hydrogen must be the internal alkyne but-2-yne. Lindlar-type hydrogenation stops at the alkene and gives cis-but-2-ene (which has cis and trans forms). Ozonolysis cleaves CH₃CH=CHCH₃ into two molecules of ethanal.
solution.why_others_wrong: Propanal and methanal come from but-1-ene, which would arise from but-1-yne (which reacts with NaNH₂); butan-2-one and butanal come from hydration, not ozonolysis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes and alkenes: reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reaction in List-I with its main product in List-II.

List-I:
A. Ethyne + H₂ (Pd/charcoal deactivated with quinoline)
B. But-2-yne + sodium in liquid ammonia
C. Ethene + H₂ (finely divided Ni)
D. Benzene + H₂ (Ni, high temperature and pressure)

List-II:
I. Cyclohexane
II. Ethane
III. trans-But-2-ene
IV. Ethene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The deactivated (Lindlar-type) catalyst stops the reduction of an alkyne at the alkene. Sodium in liquid ammonia also stops at the alkene but gives the trans isomer. Ordinary metal catalysts saturate C=C fully, and benzene adds three H₂ only under vigorous conditions.
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes giving ethane from the deactivated catalyst ignore that the catalyst is poisoned to stop at the alkene; cyclohexane does not come from an alkene of two or four carbons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes: addition of hydrogen; arenes: addition reactions
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Dihalogen derivatives with both halogen atoms on the same carbon are called geminal (gem) dihalides. How many of the following are gem-dihalides?
CH₃CHCl₂, ClCH₂–CH₂Cl, CH₃CBr₂CH₃, CH₃CHBr–CH₂Br, ClCH₂–CH₂–CH₂Cl

solution.explanation: Gem-dihalides (alkylidene halides) have both halogens on one carbon; vicinal dihalides (alkylene dihalides) have them on adjacent carbons.
steps: ClCH₂CH₂CH₂Cl: halogens on C-1 and C-3, neither
solution.why_others_wrong: Counting the vicinal compounds or the 1,3-dichloride as gem-dihalides gives 3 or 4.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', classification

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?

solution.explanation: For the same alkyl group, the boiling point rises with the size and mass of the halogen, because larger, more polarisable halogen atoms give stronger van der Waals forces: RI > RBr > RCl > RF.
steps: Molar mass and van der Waals forces: I > Br > Cl > F
solution.why_others_wrong: The C–F bond is the most polar, but polarity is not the deciding factor here; the heavier halides have the stronger intermolecular forces.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', physical properties: boiling points

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the polyhalogen compound in List-I with its use in List-II.

List-I:
A. Dichloromethane
B. Iodoform
C. Freons
D. DDT

List-II:
I. Refrigeration and air conditioning
II. Paint remover
III. Insecticide
IV. Antiseptic (formerly), acting through the free iodine it liberates

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Dichloromethane is a solvent used as a paint remover and in drug manufacture. Iodoform was used as an antiseptic because it liberates free iodine. Freons (chlorofluorocarbons) are used in refrigeration, air conditioning and as aerosol propellants. DDT was the first chlorinated organic insecticide.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping dichloromethane and iodoform, or freons and DDT, mismatches a solvent with an antiseptic or a refrigerant with an insecticide.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', polyhalogen compounds
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 1.09 g of bromoethane is boiled with excess aqueous NaOH until it is completely hydrolysed. The solution is acidified with dilute nitric acid and then titrated with 0.10 M AgNO₃. The volume of AgNO₃ solution needed to precipitate all the bromide is (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80):

solution.concept: Nucleophilic substitution releases the halide ion
solution.explanation: The C–Br bond is covalent, so bromoethane itself gives no precipitate with AgNO₃. Hydrolysis (C₂H₅Br + OH⁻ → C₂H₅OH + Br⁻) frees bromide ions; nitric acid removes the excess OH⁻, which would otherwise precipitate silver oxide.
steps: Molar mass of C₂H₅Br = 109 g mol⁻¹; n = 1.09/109 = 0.010 mol
solution.why_others_wrong: 50 mL and 200 mL use a 1 : 2 or 2 : 1 ratio; 10 mL is a tenfold slip in the conversion to mL.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nucleophilic substitution reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Allylic and benzylic halides show high reactivity towards the SN1 reaction.
Reason (R): The allylic or benzylic carbocation formed in the slow step is stabilised by resonance.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Reactivity of allylic and benzylic halides in SN1
solution.explanation: The rate of an SN1 reaction depends on how easily the carbocation forms. In CH₂=CH–CH₂⁺ and C₆H₅–CH₂⁺ the positive charge is delocalised over the double bond or the benzene ring, so these carbocations form readily. R explains A.
steps: SN1: rate-determining ionisation to a carbocation
Allyl and benzyl cations: resonance stabilised
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', SN1 mechanism
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the physical properties of haloalkanes are correct?

(a) Bromo, iodo and polychloro derivatives of hydrocarbons are heavier than water.
(b) The density of haloalkanes increases with the number of carbon atoms, the number of halogen atoms and the atomic mass of the halogen.
(c) Methyl bromide is a liquid at room temperature.
(d) Haloalkanes dissolve in organic solvents.
(e) Among isomeric haloalkanes, the boiling point increases with branching.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Density, state and solubility of haloalkanes
solution.explanation: NCERT notes that bromo, iodo and polychloro compounds are denser than water and that density rises with more carbon atoms, more halogen atoms and heavier halogens.
