Methyl chloride, methyl bromide, ethyl chloride and some chlorofluoromethanes are gases at room temperature. Haloalkanes dissolve in organic solvents. Branching lowers the surface area and hence the boiling point.
steps: (e) false: branching lowers the boiling point
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', physical properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the preparation of iodoarenes by electrophilic substitution, an oxidising agent such as HNO₃ or HIO₄ is needed, because the reaction is reversible and the HI formed must be oxidised.
Statement II: Fluoroarenes are not prepared by direct electrophilic fluorination, because fluorine is far too reactive.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Preparation of haloarenes by electrophilic substitution
solution.explanation: Chlorination and bromination of arenes with a Lewis acid catalyst work well. Iodination is reversible, so HI is removed by oxidation. Fluorine reacts too violently for controlled substitution.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', preparation of haloarenes from hydrocarbons
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Bromoethane is heated with silver nitrite to give X as the main product. X is reduced with tin and hydrochloric acid to give Y. Y is:

solution.concept: Ambident nucleophiles and reduction of nitro compounds
solution.explanation: Silver nitrite is covalent, so the nitrite ion attacks through nitrogen and gives the nitroalkane (KNO₂, which is ionic, gives the alkyl nitrite through oxygen). A nitro group is reduced to –NH₂ by a metal and acid.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ethyl nitrite would be the product with KNO₂ and gives no amine on reduction; ethanol and ethanenitrile need OH⁻ and CN⁻ respectively.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nucleophilic substitution; 'Amines', reduction of nitro compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Nitro groups ortho and para to the halogen make aryl halides much more reactive towards nucleophiles. Match the aryl chloride in List-I with the condition needed to convert it into the corresponding phenol (List-II).

List-I:
A. Chlorobenzene
B. 1-Chloro-4-nitrobenzene
C. 1-Chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene
D. 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene

List-II:
I. Warm water, 323 K
II. Aqueous NaOH, 443 K, then H⁺
III. Aqueous NaOH, 623 K and 300 atm, then H⁺
IV. Aqueous NaOH, 368 K, then H⁺

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Effect of electron-withdrawing groups on haloarenes
solution.explanation: An –NO₂ group at the ortho or para position withdraws electron density from the ring and stabilises the negatively charged intermediate (the charge can reach the nitro group by resonance). The more such groups, the milder the conditions.
steps: Three (o, o, p): warm water, 323 K (I)
solution.why_others_wrong: Any code that gives a more nitrated compound a harsher condition than a less nitrated one reverses the activating effect of the nitro groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', reactions of haloarenes: effect of substituents
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Counting the two enantiomers of a chiral compound separately, how many isomers have the molecular formula C₄H₉Cl?

solution.concept: Structural isomers and enantiomers of chlorobutanes
solution.explanation: First list the structural isomers, then look for a carbon bonded to four different groups.
steps: 2-Chlorobutane: C-2 has H, Cl, CH₃, C₂H₅ → chiral, two enantiomers
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 counts structures only; 6 or 7 wrongly treat 1-chloro-2-methylpropane (C-2 has two CH₃) or 2-chloro-2-methylpropane as chiral.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', optical isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Formalin, a 40% aqueous solution of methanal, is mainly used:

options.text: as a fuel in spirit lamps

solution.explanation: NCERT lists formalin (about 40% methanal in water) as the liquid used to preserve biological specimens.
solution.why_others_wrong: Sodium benzoate, not formalin, is the common food preservative; formalin is neither a paint solvent nor a lamp fuel.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', uses of aldehydes and ketones
solution.final_answer: Option D: to preserve biological specimens

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ketones are prepared by treating acyl chlorides with dialkylcadmium: 2CH₃COCl + (CH₃)₂Cd → 2CH₃COCH₃ + CdCl₂. The mass of propanone obtained from 15.7 g of ethanoyl chloride, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, Cl = 35.5):

solution.concept: Preparation of ketones from acyl chlorides
solution.explanation: Each molecule of acyl chloride gives one molecule of ketone; the dialkylcadmium supplies one alkyl group to each.
steps: Molar mass of CH₃COCl = 78.5 g mol⁻¹; n = 15.7/78.5 = 0.20 mol
solution.why_others_wrong: 5.8 g takes the 2 : 1 ratio the wrong way; 23.2 g doubles the moles; 15.7 g assumes equal masses.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', preparation of ketones from acyl chlorides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the substance in List-I with its use in List-II.

List-I:
A. Methanoic acid
B. Ethanoic acid
C. Sodium benzoate
D. Sodium or potassium salts of higher fatty acids

List-II:
I. Soaps and detergents
II. Rubber, textile, dyeing, leather and electroplating industries
III. Food preservative
IV. Solvent, and as vinegar in the food industry

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Uses of carboxylic acids and their salts
solution.explanation: These are the uses NCERT gives: methanoic acid in rubber, textile, dyeing, leather and electroplating; ethanoic acid as a solvent and as vinegar; sodium benzoate as a food preservative; and salts of higher fatty acids as soaps.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping methanoic and ethanoic acids, or the preservative and soaps, mismatches the uses.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', uses of carboxylic acids
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The miscibility of ethers with water resembles that of alcohols of the same molecular mass.
Statement II: Ether molecules are associated through intermolecular hydrogen bonds, as alcohol molecules are.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Solubility and boiling points of ethers
solution.explanation: Ethers can accept hydrogen bonds from water through the lone pairs on oxygen, so ethoxyethane and butan-1-ol are miscible with water to almost the same extent. But ethers have no O–H group, so their molecules cannot hydrogen bond with one another; this is why their boiling points are much lower than those of isomeric alcohols.
steps: Statement I: true (ethoxyethane ≈ butan-1-ol in miscibility)
Statement II: false; no O–H in ethers
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', physical properties of ethers
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Phenol dissolves in aqueous sodium hydroxide.
Reason (R): Phenol reacts with bromine water to give a white precipitate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Phenol is acidic enough to react with NaOH and form the soluble salt sodium phenoxide. R is a true reaction of phenol (bromination of the activated ring to 2,4,6-tribromophenol), but it is about ring substitution, not acidity, so it does not explain A.
steps: R: electrophilic substitution, unrelated to A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', acidity of phenols; electrophilic substitution
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the conversion in List-I with the conditions used for it in List-II.

List-I:
A. Ethanol → ethene
B. A secondary alcohol → alkene
C. A tertiary alcohol → alkene
D. Ethanol (in excess) → ethoxyethane

List-II:
I. 20% H₃PO₄, 358 K
II. Concentrated H₂SO₄, 443 K
III. Concentrated H₂SO₄, 413 K
IV. 85% H₃PO₄, 440 K

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The ease of dehydration is tertiary > secondary > primary, so the conditions needed become milder from primary to tertiary. With ethanol in excess and a lower temperature (413 K), intermolecular dehydration gives the ether.
steps: Ether from ethanol: conc. H₂SO₄, 413 K (III)
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that give the tertiary alcohol the harshest conditions reverse the order of ease of dehydration; 443 K versus 413 K decides alkene versus ether for ethanol.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', reactions of alcohols: dehydration
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ethanoic acid reacts with ammonia to give ammonium ethanoate, which on strong heating loses water to give ethanamide. The mass of ethanamide obtained from 7.7 g of ammonium ethanoate, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16):

solution.concept: Formation of amides from carboxylic acids
solution.explanation: CH₃COOH + NH₃ ⇌ CH₃COONH₄; on heating, CH₃COONH₄ → CH₃CONH₂ + H₂O. One mole of salt gives one mole of amide.
steps: Molar mass of CH₃COONH₄ = 77 g mol⁻¹; n = 7.7/77 = 0.10 mol
Molar mass of CH₃CONH₂ = 59 g mol⁻¹
solution.why_others_wrong: 7.7 g ignores the loss of water; 6.0 g is the mass of ethanoic acid; 4.5 g subtracts the ammonia instead of water.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', reactions of carboxylic acids: with ammonia

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following alcohols give a ketone on oxidation with acidified potassium dichromate?
Propan-2-ol, butan-2-ol, cyclohexanol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol, propan-1-ol, pentan-3-ol, benzyl alcohol

solution.concept: Oxidation of primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols
solution.explanation: Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones. Primary alcohols give aldehydes and then carboxylic acids; tertiary alcohols resist oxidation under these conditions.
steps: Secondary: propan-2-ol, butan-2-ol, cyclohexanol, pentan-3-ol → ketones
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 usually misses cyclohexanol (a secondary ring alcohol); 5 counts benzyl alcohol or the tertiary alcohol.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', oxidation of alcohols

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): o-Nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol can be separated by steam distillation, o-nitrophenol passing over with the steam.
Reason (R): o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas p-nitrophenol molecules are associated through intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Hydrogen bonding and volatility of nitrophenols
solution.explanation: Nitration of phenol with dilute nitric acid gives a mixture of o- and p-nitrophenols. In the ortho isomer the –OH and –NO₂ groups are hydrogen bonded within the molecule, so it is not associated and is steam volatile. The para isomer is held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds and is much less volatile. R explains A.
steps: o-Nitrophenol: intramolecular H-bond → volatile in steam
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', electrophilic substitution in phenols: nitration
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Carboxylic acids do not give the characteristic nucleophilic addition reactions of aldehydes and ketones, although they contain a C=O group.
Reason (R): The carbonyl carbon of a carboxylic acid is sp³ hybridised.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The carboxyl carbon is sp² hybridised and lies in a planar group, just as in aldehydes and ketones. It is less electrophilic because the lone pair on the –OH oxygen is delocalised onto the C=O group by resonance, so carboxylic acids do not show typical carbonyl reactions. A is true; R is false.
steps: Carboxyl carbon: three σ bonds + one π bond → sp²
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', structure of the carboxyl group
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Propanal is treated with dilute NaOH and the aldol formed is heated. The final product is:

solution.explanation: The α-carbon of one propanal molecule (C-2) adds to the carbonyl carbon of another, giving 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal. On heating, water is lost between the α and β carbons to give the α,β-unsaturated aldehyde.
solution.why_others_wrong: Hex-2-enal and 3-hydroxyhexanal would need the bond to form at the terminal CH₃, which is not the α-carbon; in 2-methylpent-3-enal the double bond is not conjugated with C=O.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', aldol condensation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Aldehydes react with one equivalent of a monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry HCl to give a hemiacetal, which reacts with a second molecule of alcohol to give an acetal.
Statement II: Acetals and ketals are hydrolysed by aqueous mineral acids back to the corresponding aldehydes and ketones.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Dry HCl protonates the carbonyl oxygen and makes the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic, so the weak nucleophile ROH can add (hemiacetal); a second ROH replaces the –OH (acetal, a gem-dialkoxy compound). With aqueous acid the reaction runs backwards and the carbonyl compound is regenerated.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', addition of alcohols
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many of the structural isomers with the molecular formula C₅H₁₂O are primary alcohols (and so can be oxidised to aldehydes)?

solution.explanation: There are eight alcohols C₅H₁₁OH. An alcohol is primary when the –OH carbon is attached to only one other carbon (–CH₂OH).
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 misses 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol (neopentyl alcohol), which is primary although its neighbouring carbon is quaternary; 5 adds a secondary alcohol; 8 counts all alcohols.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', classification and oxidation of alcohols

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When (CH₃)₃C–Br is heated with sodium methoxide, the main product is 2-methylpropene and not tert-butyl methyl ether.
Reason (R): Alkoxides are strong bases as well as nucleophiles, and with a tertiary alkyl halide elimination competes over substitution.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Williamson synthesis works best with primary alkyl halides. A tertiary halide is crowded, so the alkoxide removes a β-hydrogen instead of attacking carbon, and an alkene is formed. tert-Butyl methyl ether is therefore made from sodium tert-butoxide and bromomethane. R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', preparation of ethers: Williamson synthesis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match each pair of compounds in List-I with the test in List-II that distinguishes them. Use each test once.

List-I:
A. Ethanal and propanone
B. Ethanol and methanol
C. Phenol and ethanol
D. Ethanoic acid and phenol

List-II:
I. Effervescence with aqueous NaHCO₃
II. Tollens' reagent
III. Iodoform test (I₂ and NaOH)
IV. White precipitate with bromine water

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Tollens' reagent is reduced by ethanal but not by propanone (both give iodoform, so that test fails here). Ethanol gives iodoform and methanol does not. Phenol gives a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol with bromine water; ethanol does not. Ethanoic acid is strong enough to liberate CO₂ from NaHCO₃; phenol is not. Once ethanol/methanol has taken the iodoform test, phenol/ethanol must take bromine water and the acid/phenol pair NaHCO₃.
solution.why_others_wrong: Iodoform cannot distinguish ethanal from propanone; NaHCO₃ cannot distinguish phenol from ethanol, as neither reacts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids' and 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', chemical tests
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following compounds give BOTH a positive iodoform test and an orange-yellow precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine?

(a) Ethanal
(b) Propanal
(c) Butan-2-one
(d) Ethanol
(e) Acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: 2,4-DNP reacts with the C=O group of aldehydes and ketones. The iodoform test needs a CH₃CO– group (or a CH₃CH(OH)– group, which is first oxidised to it).
steps: (a) ethanal: CH₃CHO, C=O and CH₃CO– → both
(d) ethanol: iodoform yes, but no C=O → no 2,4-DNP
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', haloform reaction; reactions with ammonia derivatives

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about reactions of carboxylic acids are correct?

(a) With PCl₅, a carboxylic acid gives the acyl chloride, POCl₃ and HCl.
(b) Thionyl chloride is preferred for making acyl chlorides, because the other two products are gases that escape.
(c) With PCl₃, a carboxylic acid gives the acyl chloride and H₃PO₃.
(d) Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols by sodium borohydride.
(e) On heating with P₂O₅, a carboxylic acid gives the acid anhydride.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Reactions of the –OH part of the carboxyl group
solution.explanation: The –OH of a carboxylic acid is replaced by Cl with PCl₅, PCl₃ or SOCl₂ (SO₂ and HCl escape, leaving a pure product). Strong dehydrating agents such as P₂O₅ give anhydrides. Carboxylic acids are reduced by LiAlH₄ or diborane; NaBH₄ does not reduce the carboxyl group.
steps: (a) RCOOH + PCl₅ → RCOCl + POCl₃ + HCl: true
(b) RCOOH + SOCl₂ → RCOCl + SO₂ + HCl: true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', chemical reactions of carboxylic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of benzylamine, C₆H₅–CH₂–NH₂, is:

solution.explanation: The –NH₂ group is on the CH₂ carbon, so the parent is methanamine and the phenyl group is a substituent on that carbon: phenylmethanamine. Benzenamine is aniline, where –NH₂ is on the ring.
solution.why_others_wrong: Benzenamine is C₆H₅NH₂; 'N-phenyl' would put the phenyl group on nitrogen (C₆H₅NHCH₃); 2-phenylethanamine has two CH₂ groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following are primary amines?
(CH₃)₃C–NH₂, CH₃–NH–CH₃, C₆H₅NH₂, C₆H₅CH₂NH₂, (C₂H₅)₃N, CH₃CH₂NH₂

solution.explanation: An amine is primary, secondary or tertiary according to the number of hydrogen atoms of ammonia replaced by alkyl or aryl groups (one, two or three), not according to the kind of carbon atom attached to nitrogen.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 usually treats (CH₃)₃CNH₂ as tertiary because its carbon is tertiary; 5 or 6 count the secondary or tertiary amine.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', structure and classification

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The lower aliphatic amines are gases with a fishy odour, and primary amines with three or more carbon atoms are liquids.
Statement II: The higher amines are highly soluble in water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT describes the lower aliphatic amines as gases with a fishy smell; primary amines with three or more carbon atoms are liquids and still higher ones solids. Solubility in water falls as the hydrophobic alkyl part grows, so the higher amines are essentially insoluble.
steps: Statement II: false; solubility decreases with increasing molar mass
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', physical properties
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following amines can be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?
Ethanamine, propan-1-amine, benzylamine, aniline, N-methylethanamine, triethylamine

solution.explanation: Potassium phthalimide is alkylated by an alkyl halide and the product is hydrolysed, so only primary amines are obtained. Aromatic primary amines cannot be made this way because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion. Benzyl chloride is an alkyl-type halide and reacts normally.
steps: Yes: ethanamine, propan-1-amine, benzylamine (primary, from alkyl or benzyl halides)
No: aniline (aryl halide unreactive), N-methylethanamine (2°), triethylamine (3°)
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 wrongly excludes benzylamine; 4 or 5 include aniline or a secondary/tertiary amine.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', preparation: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Aniline does not undergo the Friedel–Crafts reaction.
Reason (R): Aniline forms a salt with the Lewis acid AlCl₃; the nitrogen then carries a positive charge and acts as a strongly deactivating group.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Why aniline fails in Friedel–Crafts reactions
solution.explanation: The basic –NH₂ group donates its lone pair to AlCl₃. The resulting positively charged nitrogen withdraws electrons from the ring, so the ring is deactivated and no alkylation or acylation occurs. R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', electrophilic substitution in aromatic amines
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the gaseous phase, where solvation is absent, the basic strength of the methyl-substituted amines and ammonia follows the order:

solution.concept: Basicity of amines in the gas phase
solution.explanation: In the gas phase only the +I effect of the alkyl groups matters: each methyl group pushes electron density onto nitrogen, so tertiary > secondary > primary > NH₃. In water, solvation of the ammonium ions and steric factors change the order to (CH₃)₂NH > CH₃NH₂ > (CH₃)₃N > NH₃.
solution.why_others_wrong: (CH₃)₂NH > CH₃NH₂ > (CH₃)₃N > NH₃ is the order in aqueous solution; the other two orders ignore the +I effect.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', basic character of amines

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the test in List-I with the observation in List-II.

List-I:
A. A primary amine warmed with chloroform and ethanolic KOH
B. Aniline treated with NaNO₂ and HCl at 273–278 K, then with phenol in mildly alkaline solution
C. N-Methylethanamine shaken with benzenesulphonyl chloride
D. Aniline treated with bromine water at room temperature

List-II:
I. White precipitate
II. Foul-smelling product
III. Orange dye
IV. Product insoluble in aqueous alkali

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Primary amines give foul-smelling isocyanides (carbylamine test). Aniline is diazotised and the diazonium salt couples with phenol to give orange p-hydroxyazobenzene. A secondary amine gives an N,N-dialkylsulphonamide, which has no acidic H on nitrogen and is insoluble in alkali. Aniline and bromine water give a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.
solution.why_others_wrong: Codes that give the secondary amine a white precipitate or the coupling reaction a foul smell mix up the tests.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', chemical reactions and tests
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
1,3,5-Tribromobenzene cannot be made by direct bromination of benzene, but it can be made from aniline. Which of the following statements about this conversion are correct?

(a) Aniline reacts with bromine water at room temperature to give 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.
(b) 2,4,6-Tribromoaniline is diazotised with NaNO₂ and HCl at 273–278 K.
(c) The diazonium group is then replaced by hydrogen using hypophosphorous acid (H₃PO₂).
(d) Direct bromination of benzene with excess Br₂ and FeBr₃ gives 1,3,5-tribromobenzene, because bromine is a meta-directing group.
(e) In bromine water, the –NH₂ group directs bromine mainly to the meta positions.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Using the –NH₂ group as a temporary directing group
solution.explanation: Bromine on a benzene ring is ortho/para directing, so direct bromination cannot give the 1,3,5 pattern. The strongly activating, ortho/para-directing –NH₂ group places three Br atoms at 2, 4 and 6, which are mutually meta. The –NH₂ group is then removed: diazotisation followed by H₃PO₂ replaces –N₂⁺ by –H.
steps: (c) true: ArN₂⁺ + H₃PO₂ + H₂O → ArH + N₂ + H₃PO₃ + H⁺
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', diazonium salts: replacement by hydrogen; bromination of aniline

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Benzenediazonium chloride is prepared at 273–278 K and used immediately after preparation.
Reason (R): Benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol to give an orange azo dye.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Stability and reactions of diazonium salts
solution.explanation: Arenediazonium salts are stable only for a short time and only at low temperature, so they are made in ice-cold solution and used at once. R states a true reaction of the salt (coupling), but coupling has nothing to do with why the salt must be kept cold and used immediately.
steps: R: true (coupling reaction), not the reason for A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', diazonium salts: preparation and properties
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Benzamide is reduced with lithium aluminium hydride to give X. X is treated with NaNO₂ and dilute HCl. The main organic product is:

solution.concept: Reduction of amides; nitrous acid and primary amines
solution.explanation: LiAlH₄ reduces the amide C=O to CH₂ without losing carbon, so benzamide gives benzylamine, C₆H₅CH₂NH₂, a primary amine with –NH₂ on an sp³ carbon. Like aliphatic primary amines, it reacts with nitrous acid with loss of N₂ to give the alcohol. (Hofmann degradation with Br₂/NaOH would instead give aniline, which forms a stable diazonium salt.)
solution.why_others_wrong: Aniline, its diazonium salt and phenol all come from the Hofmann route, which removes the carbonyl carbon; LiAlH₄ keeps it.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', preparation by reduction of amides; reaction with nitrous acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following vitamins are fat soluble?
A, B₁, C, D, E, K, B₁₂

solution.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble and are stored in the liver and adipose tissue. The B group vitamins and vitamin C are water soluble.
steps: Fat soluble: A, D, E, K
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 leaves out one of A, D, E, K; 5 or 6 wrongly include vitamin B₁₂ or C.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', classification of vitamins

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Increased blood clotting time is caused by a deficiency of:

solution.explanation: NCERT's table of vitamins links vitamin K deficiency with an increased blood clotting time.
steps: Vitamin K: needed for normal blood clotting
solution.why_others_wrong: Vitamin A deficiency causes xerophthalmia and night blindness, vitamin B₁ deficiency beri beri, and vitamin D deficiency rickets and osteomalacia.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', vitamins: deficiency diseases

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the α-helix, a polypeptide chain twists into a right-handed screw, with the –NH group of each amino acid residue hydrogen bonded to the >C=O of an adjacent turn.
Statement II: In the β-pleated sheet, the peptide chains are stretched out nearly to their maximum extension and laid side by side, held together by intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: These are NCERT's descriptions of the two common secondary structures. In both, hydrogen bonds between the –NH and >C=O groups of peptide bonds hold the shape.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', structure of proteins: secondary structure
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: One mole each of maltose, sucrose and lactose is hydrolysed completely. The total number of moles of D-glucose formed is:

solution.explanation: Maltose is made of two glucose units; sucrose of one glucose and one fructose unit; lactose of one galactose and one glucose unit.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 counts maltose as giving only one glucose; 2 or 1 forget the glucose units in sucrose or lactose.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', disaccharides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the name D-(+)-glucose, the sign '(+)' indicates that glucose:

options.text: has its –OH group on the right at the lowest asymmetric carbon
is dextrorotatory, rotating plane-polarised light to the right
has a positive charge in solution

solution.explanation: The letter D refers to the configuration (related to glyceraldehyde), while (+) or (−) gives the experimentally observed direction of optical rotation. The two are independent: D-fructose, for example, is laevorotatory.
solution.why_others_wrong: The –OH on the right at the lowest asymmetric carbon is what 'D' means, not '(+)'; the sign says nothing about reducing behaviour or charge.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', glucose: D- and L- configuration
solution.final_answer: Option B: is dextrorotatory, rotating plane-polarised light to the right

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Glucose pentaacetate does not react with hydroxylamine.
Reason (R): In the pentaacetate the –OH at C-1 of the cyclic (hemiacetal) form is acetylated, so the ring cannot open to give a free –CHO group.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Evidence for the cyclic structure of glucose
solution.explanation: Glucose itself forms an oxime because its ring opens to the free aldehyde in solution. In the pentaacetate the anomeric –OH is converted into an acetate, the hemiacetal cannot open, and no free –CHO is available. NCERT uses this as evidence for the cyclic structure. R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', cyclic structure of glucose
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the carbohydrate in List-I with the glycosidic linkage found in it (List-II).

List-I:
A. Maltose
B. Lactose
C. Sucrose
D. Amylopectin (at the branch points)

List-II:
I. C1 of α-D-glucose to C2 of β-D-fructose
II. C1–C6 linkage between α-D-glucose units
III. C1 of α-D-glucose to C4 of another glucose unit
IV. C1 of β-D-galactose to C4 of β-D-glucose

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Glycosidic linkages in di- and polysaccharides
solution.explanation: Maltose: two α-D-glucose units, C1–C4. Lactose: β-D-galactose and β-D-glucose, C1 of galactose to C4 of glucose. Sucrose: C1 of α-D-glucose to C2 of β-D-fructose, which uses both reducing groups. Amylopectin: C1–C4 in the chains and C1–C6 at the branches.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping maltose and lactose ignores that lactose contains galactose; sucrose is the only one with a C1–C2 linkage.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', disaccharides and polysaccharides
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sucrose is dextrorotatory, but after hydrolysis the solution becomes laevorotatory.
Reason (R): Both glucose and fructose are laevorotatory.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Hydrolysis gives equal amounts of D-(+)-glucose (+52.5°) and D-(−)-fructose (−92.4°). Fructose has the larger rotation, so the mixture is laevorotatory and the change in sign is called inversion. Glucose itself is dextrorotatory, so R is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', sucrose: invert sugar
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the term in List-I with its description in List-II.

List-I:
A. Nucleoside
B. Nucleotide
C. Phosphodiester linkage
D. Complementary base pairing

List-II:
I. Joins the 5′ and 3′ carbon atoms of the pentose sugars of successive nucleotides
II. Base + sugar + phosphoric acid (at the 5′ position of the sugar)
III. Adenine with thymine and guanine with cytosine, through hydrogen bonds
IV. Base attached to C-1′ of the sugar

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A nucleoside is a base joined at the 1′ position of the sugar; a nucleotide also has a phosphate at the 5′ position. Nucleotides are joined by phosphodiester links between C-5′ and C-3′ of the sugars, and the two strands of DNA are held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary bases.
solution.why_others_wrong: Confusing nucleoside and nucleotide misses the phosphate group; the phosphodiester link joins sugars, not bases.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids: chemical composition and structure
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about carbohydrates are correct?

(a) Carbohydrates that yield two to ten monosaccharide units on hydrolysis are called oligosaccharides.
(b) Glucose occurs freely in nature as well as in combined form.
(c) Starch is the main storage polysaccharide of plants.
(d) Sucrose is a reducing sugar.
(e) Monosaccharides can be hydrolysed further into simpler polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Oligosaccharides give 2–10 monosaccharide units on hydrolysis. Glucose is found free (in fruits, honey) and combined (in sucrose, starch, cellulose). Starch is the main storage polysaccharide of plants. Sucrose is non-reducing because the reducing groups of both units form the glycosidic bond, and monosaccharides cannot be hydrolysed further.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', carbohydrates: classification

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Mohr's salt, FeSO₄·(NH₄)₂SO₄·6H₂O (molar mass 392 g mol⁻¹), is prepared by crystallising an equimolar solution of ferrous sulphate and ammonium sulphate. The maximum mass of Mohr's salt that can be obtained from 2.78 g of FeSO₄·7H₂O (molar mass 278 g mol⁻¹) with excess ammonium sulphate is:

solution.explanation: One mole of FeSO₄·7H₂O gives one mole of the double salt, which crystallises with six molecules of water.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.78 g assumes equal masses; 1.96 g and 7.84 g halve or double the moles.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of double salts: Mohr's salt

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Detection of elements and functional groups
questions.question_text: A sample is heated with a little solid potassium hydrogensulphate, and a pungent, irritating smell of acrolein is noticed. The sample is most likely:

solution.explanation: On heating with KHSO₄ (a dehydrating agent), the glycerol part of a fat or oil is dehydrated to acrolein (propenal), which has a sharp, irritating smell. This acrolein test identifies fats and oils.
solution.why_others_wrong: Proteins and amino acids are tested by the biuret and ninhydrin tests, carbohydrates by Molisch's test.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), tests for carbohydrates, fats and proteins
solution.final_answer: Option C: a fat or oil

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 25.0 mL of an oxalic acid solution needs 20.0 mL of 0.020 M KMnO₄ for complete reaction in dilute H₂SO₄. The strength of the oxalic acid solution, expressed as grams of crystalline oxalic acid, H₂C₂O₄·2H₂O, per litre, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.explanation: In acid, 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O, so 2 mol MnO₄⁻ react with 5 mol oxalic acid.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3.60 g L⁻¹ uses the anhydrous molar mass (90); 2.02 g L⁻¹ takes a 1 : 1 mole ratio; 12.6 g L⁻¹ takes the solution as 0.1 M.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric exercises: oxalic acid vs KMnO₄

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the titration of oxalic acid with KMnO₄, the first few drops of permanganate are decolourised slowly, but later drops are decolourised almost at once.
Reason (R): The Mn²⁺ ions formed in the reaction catalyse the reaction between permanganate and oxalic acid (autocatalysis).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: At the start no Mn²⁺ is present and the reaction is slow even in warm solution. As soon as some Mn²⁺ forms, it catalyses the reaction, so it speeds up. R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titration of oxalic acid with potassium permanganate
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
In systematic salt analysis, how many of the following cations are precipitated in group II, as sulphides by H₂S in the presence of dilute HCl?
Cu²⁺, Cd²⁺, As³⁺, Zn²⁺, Ni²⁺, Al³⁺, Ba²⁺

solution.explanation: In dilute HCl the sulphide ion concentration is kept low (common ion effect on H₂S), so only the sulphides with very low solubility products (group II) precipitate. Zn²⁺ and Ni²⁺ come down as sulphides only in ammoniacal solution (group IV); Al³⁺ is precipitated as hydroxide in group III and Ba²⁺ as carbonate in group V.
steps: Group III: Al³⁺; group IV: Zn²⁺, Ni²⁺; group V: Ba²⁺
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 wrongly places Zn²⁺ or Ni²⁺ in group II; 1 or 2 miss Cd²⁺ or As³⁺.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), qualitative analysis of cations

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Iodoform is prepared in the laboratory by warming ethanol with iodine and aqueous NaOH:
C₂H₅OH + 4I₂ + 6NaOH → CHI₃ + HCOONa + 5NaI + 5H₂O
For complete conversion of 2.3 g of ethanol, the minimum mass of iodine needed and the mass of iodoform formed are, respectively (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, I = 127):

solution.explanation: Ethanol is first oxidised to ethanal by the hypoiodite (one I₂), and the CH₃ group of ethanal is then tri-iodinated (three I₂) before cleavage, so 4 mol I₂ are used per mole of ethanol.
solution.why_others_wrong: 12.7 g uses one I₂ per ethanol; 38.1 g uses three (forgets the oxidation step); 39.4 g doubles the iodoform.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of iodoform

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the kinetics experiments in the laboratory are correct?

(a) In the reaction of sodium thiosulphate with hydrochloric acid, the time for a cross mark under the flask to disappear is taken as inversely proportional to the rate.
(b) In that reaction, the turbidity is due to colloidal sulphur formed in the reaction.
(c) In the iodide–hydrogen peroxide clock reaction with starch and a little thiosulphate, the blue colour appears only after all the added thiosulphate has been used up.
(d) Raising the temperature increases the time taken for the cross to disappear.
(e) Starch acts as a catalyst in the iodide–hydrogen peroxide reaction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Following reaction rates by a visual end point
solution.explanation: Na₂S₂O₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + SO₂ + S + H₂O: the sulphur makes the solution turbid, and the faster the reaction the sooner the cross is hidden, so rate ∝ 1/t. In the clock reaction, the iodine formed is reduced back to iodide by thiosulphate; only when the thiosulphate is used up does iodine remain and give the blue starch–iodine colour. Starch is only an indicator. A higher temperature speeds up the reaction and shortens the time.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), chemical kinetics experiments
